local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 every West Virginia county elects a county commissioner, and voters fill any unexpired terms of county clerk, circuit clerk, prosecuting attorney, sheriff, assessor, magistrate and county board of education; some cities and towns elect their officers that day too. Full terms of sheriff, prosecuting attorney, assessor and surveyor are elected in presidential years and both clerks every six years (all next in 2028), while magistrates (next in 2028), county boards of education and conservation district supervisors are elected on the nonpartisan ballot at the May primary, held May 12 this year. Other cities and towns voted with the May primary or vote on their own dates (the Secretary of State publishes calendars for town elections on June 2 and June 9, 2026); state law has every one of them move to a statewide primary or general election day by July 1, 2032.
local_calendar.s: W. Va. Code sections 3-1-17, 18-5-1b, 18-5-2, 19-21A-6, 3-1-31 and 8-5-5 (West Virginia Legislature); the Secretary of State's 2026 municipal election calendars

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Secretary of State's 2026 General Candidate Listing at the county level: 55 county commission races in 54 of the 55 counties, 31 unexpired terms of county offices and magistrate, 3 county board of education races and 9 town races in Cowen town, North Hills town and Pax town: 163 candidates, 3 of them declared write-ins. Left out: 139 candidates for town offices that the list files under Kanawha, Logan, Marion and Putnam counties without naming the town; the county commission race in Webster County, where the list has no candidate; towns that are not on the Secretary's list at all; ballot questions and levies; and party committee seats. The list gives no ballot order and no longer lists anyone who withdrew, and the magisterial district that the ballot prints beside commission and school board candidates (it is where the candidate lives) is not shown.
local_coverage.s: West Virginia Secretary of State, 2026 General Candidate Listing (county-level offices)

gaps.r: The Secretary of State's list files 55 candidates for council member, mayor, municipal judge and recorder under Kanawha County but names the town for only 16 of them (Charleston city and Chesapeake town); the others carry a ward, a term or nothing where the town should be, so the list cannot say which town each is running in, and none of the county's town races is shown. The county's sample ballots will show them.

The Secretary of State's list files 14 candidates for council member, mayor and recorder under Logan County without naming the town for any of them, so it cannot say which town each is running in. The county's sample ballots will show them.

The Secretary of State's list files 12 candidates for council member under Marion County without naming the town for any of them, so it cannot say which town each is running in. The county's sample ballots will show them.

The Secretary of State's list files 58 candidates for council member, mayor and recorder under Putnam County without naming the town for any of them, so it cannot say which town each is running in. The county's sample ballots will show them.

State law has every county elect a commissioner at each general election, and the official results of the May 12 primary show Democrat and Republican candidates for the office in Webster County, but the Secretary of State's November list carries no candidate for County Commission there, so the race cannot be shown yet.

gaps.w: city and town races that are not on the Secretary of State's list
gaps.r: Cities and towns take their own candidate filings, and the Secretary of State's list carries town offices under only seven counties, so a town that votes on November 3 without appearing there is not here.
